topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: What is the maximum fine the State Real Estate Commission may levy against a licensee found guilty of a RELRA Section 604 violation, in addition to (or instead of) suspending or revoking the license?
explanation: RELRA Section 604(a) authorizes the Commission, after a hearing, to refuse, suspend, or revoke a license or registration certificate, or to levy fines not exceeding $1,000, or both, for any of the Section 604 prohibited acts.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Acting for more than one party to a transaction is prohibited under RELRA Section 604(7) UNLESS what condition is met?
choice_a: The licensee discloses the dual role only if directly asked
choice_c: The licensee has the knowledge and written consent of all parties for whom he acts
choice_d: Both parties are represented by separate attorneys
explanation: Section 604(7) makes it a disciplinable act to represent more than one party to a transaction 'without the knowledge and consent in writing of all parties for whom he acts' -- written, informed consent from every represented party is the safe harbor.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under RELRA Section 604(8), what must a broker obtain before placing a 'for sale' or 'for rent' sign on, or advertising, a property?
choice_a: Approval from the local municipality's zoning office
choice_b: A permit from the Real Estate Commission for each sign
choice_c: Nothing -- no owner consent is required under RELRA
choice_d: The written consent of the owner or the owner's authorized agent
explanation: Section 604(8) makes it a disciplinable act to place a for-sale/for-rent sign on, or advertise, a property without the written consent of the owner or the owner's authorized agent.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: If a broker or salesperson wants to purchase, or acquire an option on, property that has been listed with their own office, what must they do first?
choice_a: Disclose to the owner in writing their intention or true position before (directly or indirectly, even through a third party) acquiring such an interest
choice_b: Nothing -- licensees are categorically barred from ever purchasing listed property
choice_c: Obtain a waiver from the Real Estate Commission on a case-by-case basis
choice_d: Wait until the listing has expired for at least 6 months
explanation: RELRA Section 604(13) requires written disclosure to the owner of the licensee's true position before purchasing or otherwise acquiring an interest in listed property, whether the acquisition is direct or accomplished indirectly through a third party.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Conviction of which category of crimes is expressly listed in RELRA Section 604(14) as grounds for license discipline?
choice_a: Only traffic violations related to DUI
choice_b: Forgery, embezzlement, obtaining money under false pretenses, bribery, larceny, extortion, conspiracy to defraud, or similar offenses, or any felony
choice_c: Only offenses committed while actively licensed and working a transaction
choice_d: Only convictions in a Pennsylvania court, excluding other states or federal courts
explanation: Section 604(14) covers convictions (including guilty or nolo contendere pleas) 'in this or any other state, or Federal court' for forgery, embezzlement, obtaining money under false pretenses, bribery, larceny, extortion, conspiracy to defraud, similar offenses, or any felony -- a broad, multi-jurisdictional standard.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: What is the umbrella 'catch-all' disciplinary standard found at RELRA Section 604(20)?
choice_a: Any violation must independently match one of the other 22 enumerated paragraphs; there is no catch-all standard
choice_b: Any conduct that generates a consumer complaint, regardless of merit
choice_c: Any conduct in a real estate transaction that demonstrates bad faith, dishonesty, untrustworthiness, or incompetency
choice_d: Any failure to attend continuing education, regardless of the underlying conduct
explanation: Section 604(20) is a broad catch-all: 'Any conduct in a real estate transaction which demonstrates bad faith, dishonesty, untrustworthiness, or incompetency' is independently disciplinable, giving the Commission flexibility beyond the specifically enumerated paragraphs.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: How does RELRA Section 604(22) coordinate discipline for housing-discrimination complaints with the Pennsylvania Human Relations Commission (PHRC)?
choice_a: The State Real Estate Commission must always wait for a final PHRC court judgment before acting
choice_b: The PHRC has no involvement in real estate discrimination complaints at all
choice_c: The 90-day waiting period applies to every subsequent complaint against the same licensee, not just the first
choice_d: If the PHRC does not act on a discrimination complaint within 90 days after it is filed, the State Real Estate Commission may then proceed with its own action against the licensee
explanation: RELRA Section 604(22)(iii)-(iv) gives the PHRC a 90-day head start to investigate an initial discrimination complaint tied to real estate activities before the State Real Estate Commission may act; that 90-day waiting period applies only to a licensee's FIRST such complaint -- second or subsequent complaints may go directly to the Real Estate Commission.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under RELRA Section 702 (Imputed knowledge, limitations), when may a broker's license be revoked or suspended for a violation committed by an affiliated salesperson or associate broker?
choice_a: Only if it appears, upon hearing, that the broker had actual knowledge of the violation
choice_b: Automatically, any time an affiliated salesperson violates RELRA, regardless of the broker's knowledge
choice_c: Only if the broker personally profited from the violation
choice_d: Never -- brokers cannot be disciplined for a salesperson's individual misconduct under any circumstance
explanation: Section 702(a) shields a broker from vicarious license discipline for a salesperson's or associate broker's violation absent a hearing finding that the broker had actual knowledge of it -- though Section 702(c) makes a shown 'course of dealing' by the employee prima facie evidence of the employer's actual knowledge.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: What evidentiary effect does a demonstrated 'course of dealing' by a salesperson have on the question of the employing broker's knowledge, under RELRA Section 702(c)?
choice_a: It is legally irrelevant to the broker's own culpability
choice_b: It constitutes prima facie evidence of the broker's actual knowledge of the violation
choice_c: It shifts the burden of proof to the salesperson exclusively, exonerating the broker entirely
choice_d: It requires the Commission to dismiss the complaint against the broker automatically
explanation: Section 702(c) provides that a shown 'course of dealing' followed by the employee constitutes prima facie evidence of the employer's knowledge -- meaning a pattern of repeated violations can support an inference that the broker knew (or should have known) and failed to supervise adequately.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Practicing as a real estate broker in Pennsylvania without a license, for a FIRST offense, is classified and penalized how under RELRA Section 303?
choice_a: A third-degree felony on the first offense
choice_b: A civil infraction only, with no criminal exposure
choice_c: A summary offense, punishable by a fine not exceeding $500 and/or imprisonment not exceeding 3 months
choice_d: An automatic $10,000 fine with no imprisonment possible
explanation: RELRA Section 303 classifies unlicensed practice, continuing business after suspension/revocation, or employing an unlicensed salesperson as a summary offense on a FIRST offense (fine up to $500 and/or up to 3 months' imprisonment), escalating to a third-degree felony (fine of $2,000-$5,000 and/or 1-2 years' imprisonment) for a second or subsequent offense.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under RELRA Section 302, may an unlicensed person sue in Pennsylvania courts to recover compensation for real estate brokerage services they performed?
choice_a: Yes, as long as the services were actually completed successfully
choice_b: Yes, if the unlicensed person discloses their status to the paying party in advance
choice_c: Yes, but recovery is capped at the value of out-of-pocket expenses only
choice_d: No -- no action or suit for such compensation may be maintained unless the person was duly licensed at the time of offering to perform the act or procuring the promise of payment
explanation: RELRA Section 302 bars courts from allowing recovery of compensation for brokerage acts by anyone who was not duly licensed at the time they offered to perform the act or service, or procured a promise or contract for payment of compensation for it.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: What per-claim and per-licensee liability caps apply to the Pennsylvania Real Estate Recovery Fund under RELRA Section 803(d)?
choice_a: $20,000 per claim, not to exceed $100,000 total per licensee
choice_b: $5,000 per claim, not to exceed $25,000 per licensee
choice_c: $50,000 per claim with no per-licensee aggregate cap
choice_d: $100,000 per claim, not to exceed $500,000 per licensee
explanation: RELRA Section 803(d) caps the Recovery Fund's liability at $20,000 for any one claim and $100,000 total per licensee or registrant; if aggregate valid claims against one licensee exceed $100,000, the fund distributes that capped amount pro rata among the claimants.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: What happens to a licensee's license automatically once the Commission pays a claim from the Real Estate Recovery Fund on that licensee's behalf?
choice_a: Nothing changes -- the licensee's status is unaffected by a Recovery Fund payment
choice_b: The license automatically suspends upon the effective date of the fund's payment
choice_c: The license is automatically and permanently revoked with no path to reinstatement
choice_d: Only the license of any affiliated salesperson is suspended, not the paying licensee's own license
explanation: RELRA Section 803(f)(1) provides that a licensee's license automatically suspends upon the effective date of a Recovery Fund payment made on a judgment against them; reinstatement requires full repayment to the fund plus 10% annual interest under Section 803(f)(2).

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: What must an aggrieved consumer show before recovering from the Real Estate Recovery Fund, per RELRA Section 803(b)?
choice_a: Only a sworn complaint filed with the Commission, with no court judgment required
choice_b: Proof that the licensee has already been criminally convicted of fraud
choice_c: A final judgment for fraud, misrepresentation, or deceit against a licensee, exhaustion of other legal/equitable remedies, that they are not the debtor's spouse, and a timely application within 1 year of the judgment proceedings' termination
choice_d: A settlement agreement signed by the licensee's insurer
explanation: RELRA Section 803(a)-(b) requires a final judgment on grounds of fraud, misrepresentation, or deceit against a person licensed under the act, that the claimant exhausted other reasonably available legal and equitable remedies, that the claimant is not the judgment debtor's spouse, and that the application is filed within 1 year after the judgment proceedings (including appeals) conclude.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Which two categories of activity are expressly EXCLUDED from Real Estate Recovery Fund coverage under RELRA Section 801(b)?
choice_a: Residential sales transactions and property management agreements
choice_b: Commercial leasing transactions and escrow disputes
choice_c: All transactions involving a licensed associate broker
choice_d: The sale or offer to sell a campground membership, and the preparation or issuance of a broker price opinion
explanation: RELRA Section 801(b), as amended in 2018, states the Recovery Fund does not apply to the sale of, or offer to sell, a campground membership (or to a campground membership salesperson), nor to the preparation or issuance of a broker price opinion.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: How is each licensee's contribution to the Real Estate Recovery Fund structured under RELRA Section 802?
choice_a: A $10 fee is paid at license renewal and upon initial licensure/registration, with an additional per-licensee assessment (up to $10) authorized if the fund balance falls below $300,000, to restore it toward $500,000
choice_b: A flat annual $500 fee per licensee, regardless of the fund's balance
choice_c: A one-time $10 fee paid only at initial licensure, never again
explanation: Section 802 funds the Recovery Fund with a $10 fee at each biennial renewal and at initial licensure/registration, plus authority for the Commission to levy an additional assessment (capped at $10 per licensee) if, at the start of a biennial renewal period beginning in 1982 or later, the fund balance drops below $300,000 -- with the goal of restoring the balance to $500,000.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Which category of real estate professional is exempt from RELRA licensure when acting under an executed and recorded power of attorney, or when acting as an attorney at law?
choice_a: Only licensed CPAs performing real estate closings
choice_b: Services rendered by an attorney-in-fact under a properly executed and recorded power of attorney (not used to circumvent the act), or by an attorney at law
choice_c: Any unlicensed assistant working under a broker's direct supervision
choice_d: Mortgage loan originators acting within the scope of their federal license
explanation: RELRA Section 304(4) exempts services rendered by an attorney-in-fact acting under an executed and recorded power of attorney from the owner/lessor (so long as it is not used to evade the Act's licensing requirements), and services rendered by an attorney at law, from RELRA's general licensure requirement.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: An unlicensed employee hired by an owner solely to manage/maintain a multifamily residential property is exempt from RELRA licensure, PROVIDED that employee does NOT do what?
choice_b: Provide information about rental amounts or building rules
choice_c: Enter into leases on the owner's behalf, negotiate occupancy terms with tenants, or hold tenant money other than on the owner's behalf
choice_d: Work more than 40 hours per week for that owner
explanation: RELRA Section 304(10) exempts an owner's management/maintenance employee from licensure only so long as the owner (not the employee) retains authority over leases, occupancy terms, and tenant funds; the employee may still show apartments and give factual information on rents and rules without triggering licensure.
